title: Cherrapunji and Ziro (Batch 6)
selection: Batch 6. Cherrapunji (4 sections, practical_info state filler) and Ziro (3, practical_info and things_to_do filler). Adds who it's for, things to do, food, tips, etiquette, FAQs and mistakes for Sohra; overview, who it's for, best time, how to reach, etiquette, FAQs and mistakes for Ziro. Replacements for the filler sections and a fuller Ziro overview go in as pending suggestions. Nohkalikai's height differs by source (about 340 m, 350 m, 'over 1,100 feet'), so no new height is given. Incredible India's Cherrapunjee page credits the Nongkrem festival to the town; it is held near Shillong, so it is not used. meghalaya-4-days itinerary left for the audit.

overview.text:
Cherrapunji, or Sohra, sits about 50 km from Shillong and still holds the records for the most rain in a month and in a year. That rain feeds some of India's great waterfalls — Nohkalikai, India's tallest plunge waterfall, and Seven Sisters, which falls in seven segments — and the living root bridges that Khasi and Jaintia villagers grow from rubber-fig roots, some over a century old.

The classic trek starts at Tyrna and descends about 3,500 steps to Nongriat's Double Decker bridge, with Rainbow Falls further on. Closer to town are Mawsmai and Arwah caves, Khoh Ramhah and the Mawkdok Dympep valley view. November to February is drier; the monsoon makes the falls thunder. Eat jadoh and tungrymbai, and buy bamboo and cane crafts.

overview.text:
Ziro is a high valley in Arunachal Pradesh, about 1,500 m up and 165 km from Itanagar, home to the Apatani people. Their rice terraces, farmed together with fish in the same paddies, got the valley shortlisted for UNESCO World Heritage status in 2012; at Tarin Fish Farm you can see Mipya and Emoh rice grown alongside Ngihi fish.

Pine-clad hills ring the valley. Walk to Kile Pakho for views of the Eastern Himalayas, Pine Grove near Old Ziro and Siikhe Lake near Hapoli, or go further to Talley Valley Wildlife Sanctuary and the Siddheshwar Nath shrine at Kardo. The Apatani celebrate Myoko in March and Dree in July, and the four-day Ziro Festival of Music fills the valley in September. Indians need an Inner Line Permit; foreigners a Protected Area Permit.
